evidence.title: Ban on neo-Nazi White Australia party is ‘authoritarian’ and breaches constitution, high court hears

occurrences.checkable_against: High Court hearing transcript
occurrences.quote_span: “It can’t happen,” he said.
occurrences.speaker: Brendan Lim
occurrences.subject: White Australia party ban challenge

occurrences.checkable_against: High Court hearing transcript and 1951 Communist Party case judgment
occurrences.quote_span: Lawyers also argued the commonwealth does not have the power to ban political parties, citing a major cold war-era high court ruling in 1951, which overturned a ban on the Communist party of Australia.
occurrences.speaker: White Australia party lawyers
occurrences.subject: White Australia party ban challenge

occurrences.checkable_against: High Court hearing transcript
occurrences.quote_span: Acting for the government, Brendan Lim, denied the laws could be used for the “illegitimate purpose of quelling political competition”.
occurrences.speaker: Brendan Lim
occurrences.subject: White Australia party ban challenge

occurrences.checkable_against: High Court courtroom record or hearing transcript
occurrences.quote_span: Members of the White Australia party sat in the front of the courtroom’s public benches, including its leader, Tom Sewell.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: White Australia party ban challenge

occurrences.checkable_against: Commonwealth Criminal Code part 5.3B and High Court pleadings
occurrences.quote_span: The arguments centre on proving part 5.3B of the criminal code – which allows the federal police minister to recommend to the attorney general that a group is listed as a prohibited hate group – is invalid.
occurrences.speaker: White Australia party lawyers
occurrences.subject: White Australia party ban challenge

occurrences.checkable_against: High Court judgment and Australian hate-group listing legislation
occurrences.quote_span: If successful, the ruling could wind back the laws that have also banned the Islamist group Hizb ut-Tahrir.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: White Australia party ban challenge

occurrences.checkable_against: Commonwealth Criminal Code hate-group listing provisions
occurrences.quote_span: Groups can be listed if it is considered “reasonably necessary to protect the Australian community or part of the Australian community against social, psychological, physical or economic harm”.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: White Australia party ban challenge

occurrences.checkable_against: High Court hearing transcript and party pleadings
occurrences.quote_span: The far-right nationalist party is challenging the ban at the high court over two days this week, with its lawyers arguing the law breaches the implied freedom of political communication and that handing the decision to Burke breaches the separation of powers.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: White Australia party ban challenge

occurrences.checkable_against: Commonwealth written submissions in the High Court White Australia party case
occurrences.quote_span: “Forming a political party was a calculated attempt to secure legal protection for members engaging in openly racist and anti-Semitic speech,” the commonwealth said in written submissions.
occurrences.speaker: the Commonwealth
occurrences.subject: White Australia party ban challenge

occurrences.checkable_against: High Court hearing transcript
occurrences.quote_span: On Tuesday, the group’s barristers, Peter King and Shahed Sharify, argued a total ban on the party was akin to using a “sledgehammer on a nut”.
occurrences.speaker: Peter King and Shahed Sharify
occurrences.subject: White Australia party ban challenge

occurrences.checkable_against: High Court hearing transcript
occurrences.quote_span: Sharify argued the law’s breach of implied freedom of political communication was “authoritarian in nature” and suggested it could be used to ban any political party where its members had threatened or engaged in a hate crime with the assistance of the organisation.
occurrences.speaker: Shahed Sharify
occurrences.subject: White Australia party ban challenge

occurrences.checkable_against: Commonwealth Criminal Code hate-group listing provisions
occurrences.quote_span: Under the rules, Burke must receive advice from the head of Asio recommending that an organisation be considered for listing. The home affairs minister must then receive written agreement from the attorney general and brief the opposition leader.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: White Australia party ban challenge

occurrences.checkable_against: High Court hearing transcript
occurrences.quote_span: Sharify said the law’s purposes would be better served by handing that decision to a judge rather than a “busy minister who flicks through a brief and decides in two hours”.
occurrences.speaker: Shahed Sharify
occurrences.subject: White Australia party ban challenge

occurrences.checkable_against: High Court hearing transcript
occurrences.quote_span: The barrister said the banning of hate groups was determined by a politician, based on an opinion with no judicial fairness to appeal that decision.
occurrences.speaker: Shahed Sharify
occurrences.subject: White Australia party ban challenge

occurrences.checkable_against: High Court hearing transcript and anti-hate law legislative record
occurrences.quote_span: Lawyers for an outlawed neo-Nazi political party have argued anti-hate laws passed after the Bondi terror attack rely on the opinion of a politician and are “authoritarian in nature”.
occurrences.speaker: White Australia party lawyers
occurrences.subject: White Australia party ban challenge

occurrences.checkable_against: Commonwealth Criminal Code hate-group listing provisions
occurrences.quote_span: Unlike the terrorist group listing, a listed hate group cannot make a de-listing application.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: White Australia party ban challenge

occurrences.checkable_against: Commonwealth submissions in the High Court White Australia party case
occurrences.quote_span: The government is also expected to defend the anti-hate laws by arguing the party is not a political party but an arm of White Australia, itself a rebranded version of NSN.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: White Australia party ban challenge
